literal_submission.notes:
Selection rationale (unverified, archived only). Parent policy (R03, R04, R06, R08) addresses environment preservation, metric fidelity, causal overreach, and repair completeness, but it lacks any mechanism that (a) links a diagnostic observation to the specific source location and the failure it should remove, (b) anchors diagnosis to the earliest observed execution failure rather than plan length, and (c) requires a forecast threshold sized to the evidence. Both supplied cases show exactly these gaps: D-P's rationale names a first illegal walk failure and the source change (directed-link BFS plus gated precondition checks), yet outcome stayed 0/10 with forecast status contradicted; D-S posits a velocity-quadratic term from binned residuals and registers a min_delta of 1e-4 on train mse, but achieved delta was ~6.5e-7 — far below the registered threshold — while nmse moved only from 0.095917 to 0.095768 (a negligible change, so the improvement claim in C3 is itself weak). Hence R05 first (ground each diagnostic observation in a verifiable source-location change and the failure expected to vanish), R02 second (in D-P plan_length was 21 and 15 while executed_actions was 7 in both runs, so plan length is not a proxy for what executed; the earliest observed failure is the first_failed_action at index 7), R07 third (forecast thresholds in both cases were missed by orders of magnitude or flatly contradicted, indicating thresholds were not proportionate to the evidence — note R07's wording is forecasting-oriented and is a weak fit here, but it is the only threshold-discipline rule available; R04 was retained in the parent policy and is dropped for room), and R08 fourth to preserve the working parts and keep the repair complete without extra machinery. Deliberately omitted R01: although D-P's diff shows action-string and parameter-order handling, the registered failure is a missing link precondition, not a type/format/argument-order error, so R01 is not the binding constraint. R06 is retained in spirit by my C4 verdict of unknown rather than a necessity claim.

Auxiliary verdicts: C1 supported (D-P:source-diff shows different parent/child hashes and a visible diff). C2 unknown: no edit_contract exists, and the packet states source changes or execution failure alone cannot decide whether the specific intended repair was implemented. C3 contradicted: official nmse did not materially improve (0.0959173 -> 0.0957677) and the registered forecast is contradicted (actual_delta ~6.5e-07 vs min_delta 1e-4 on train mse); both registered metric facts are present, so the conjunction fails. C4 unknown: matched_interventions is empty in both cases, so necessity of the added v^2 structure is undecidable; a small or missed gain cannot establish it. I am not claiming these four rules are optimal, nor that applying them to any candidate would improve outcomes; both supplied cases are researcher-seen development data with contradicted forecasts and unverified rationales.
